items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: But all the great singers, like Carmen McRae, Sarah Vaughan, my friend Dinah Washington

ctx.x: A couple of other things I’d like to ask you. If you had some words to the wise, to say to young jazz singers coming up, about the real essence of the music, what would you share?

Well, as I said before, I’m not a technical musician as far as the written note is concerned. But what I have aspired to do, now that I’m being accepted in that gender as a jazz singer in some places, is to first of all as a vocalist, pay attention to what comes out of your mouth, what you are saying, the written word. You know as I say, technically, a lot of people who can read music can just pick up a lead sheet and sing the song. But your job is to make that song apply to someone. Try to be as true to the…

played piano. They were musicians. I couldn’t do that. So I had to pay attention to the word and the melody. And I find that to be a source of being able to handle the song. To me if I pay attention to what’s coming out at this point I just attempt to make a person listen to what I’m saying. To make it believable, you know. To have someone come up and say, “You know I’ve heard that song done a lot of times but when you sang it I really felt it,” you know. I think that is the payback for that. A lot of times I…
